plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces gain-magnitude and lag uncertainty in one step; needed to estimate steady-state input for target and how long to hold for settling.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with self-cooling is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.05 toward 0.3-0.6 with slowing slope; last-seconds slope still slightly positive if not fully settled.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Settling steady-state gain at u=0.5 and dominant time constant; needed to estimate equilibrium input for target 0.5 and how long controller must hold to settle.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order with slow cooling is right, y continues rising from ~0.395 toward 0.5-0.6 with gradually decreasing slope; last-5s slope should fall below 0.0015 toward near-zero if approaching y_ss(0.5), allowing tau and gain estimate.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Targets u=0 self-cooling behavior, ambient equilibrium, and cooling time constant symmetry, which determines how fast y falls and what steady u holds target.
experiments.expected_observation: If self-cooling first-order hypothesis is right, y will decay monotonically from ~0.497 toward ~0.05 with slowing negative slope, reaching ~0.12-0.20 after 180s with last-5s slope still negative around -0.001/s, confirming decay rate and ambient level.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests linearity and steady-state gain at a second amplitude above 0.5, which determines the precise feedforward u for target 0.5 and safe proportional gain without overshoot to 0.85.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order with ambient ~0.05, K~0.88 and tau ~130-155s is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.19 toward ~0.58, reaching ~0.44-0.49 after 180s with last-5s slope still positive ~0.0007-0.0012/s; a substantially lower end value would indicate saturation/sublinear gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Measures u=0 self-cooling rate, ambient, and pure delay from last command change, directly discriminating faster outflow (faster fall) from weaker actuator (same fall as E3) and slower/sensor (delayed fall or offset fall) to fix feedforward and integral for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If increased heat-loss (C2) is right, y will resume falling within ~12s after in-transit commands elapse, then fall faster than E3 baseline (E3: 0.497 to 0.19 in 180s, ~0.0014-0.0017/s early), reaching below ~0.15 by 180s and toward ~0.05-0.10 by 300s with steeper negative slope; if weaker-actuator-only (C1) fall will overlay E3, if slower (C3) fall will be delayed/flatter, if sensor-only (C4) shape will match E3 up to offset.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Discriminates weaker actuator (smaller initial heating slope and lower y_ss) from faster outflow (same initial slope as E1 but earlier flattening to lower y_ss) by replicating E1 u=0.5 heating from a low level, which fixes required feedforward u for target 0.5 and safe gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator C1 is right, y rises within ~6-12s of start with smaller initial slope than E1 baseline (E1: 0.051 to ~0.15 in ~40s) and reaches only ~0.28-0.34 after 240s still rising toward ~0.36-0.40 well below E2 y_ss(0.5)=0.491; if faster-outflow C2 is right initial slope matches E1 but flattens earlier to similar low steady state with shorter tau; if slower C3 rise is delayed >30s; if sensor-only C4 shape overlays E1 up to bias.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Estimates post-change DC gain and feedforward u for 0.5 and discriminates weaker-actuator (smaller b, smaller initial slope) from faster-outflow (same b, same initial slope, earlier flattening) at higher excitation.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator C1 is right, y rises within ~12s with initial slope ~0.0020/s (1.5x E6 0.0014/s) reaching ~0.45-0.50 after 110s still rising toward ~0.52-0.56; if faster-outflow C2 is right initial slope matches pre-change ~0.003/s but flattens earlier to lower ss; if slower C3 rise delayed >30s; if sensor-only shape overlays scaled baseline.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain); E1/E4/E6 all rise with heating.
With u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near y~0.05-0.10; E3 fell 0.497 to 0.196 in ~177s, E5 fell 0.475 to 0.105 in 300s.
Dominant time constant ~120-155s; E1 slope 0.0015 after 180s, E2 settled after ~320s, E3 tau ~152s, E5 tau ~151s, E6 rise still 0.0012/s after 240s.
No large pure delay: E1 rose within ~9s, E4 within ~9-12s, E5 fell within 5s, E6 rose within ~12s (1198-1210) from COMMAND LAST CHANGED.
Pre-change steady-state approx linear K~0.88: y_ss(0.5)~0.491, u=0.6 rising toward ~0.58, so u~0.51 held 0.5.
Sensor noise small <0.02 with ~0.005 quantization steps; E5/E6 steps same as baseline, no spikes.

Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller heating slope and lower y_ss, but u=0 cooling tau/delay unchanged; E6 0.1045 to 0.298 in 180s vs E1 0.051 to 0.395, initial slope ~0.00144 vs ~0.00242/s.
Change is faster outflow: u=0 cooling faster and tau shorter and same u holds lower y; E5 180s ratio 0.306 vs E3 0.313 gives tau ~151 vs 152s, not faster.
Change is slower response: delay much longer than 9-12s baseline and/or tau larger; E5 immediate fall and E6 12s rise refute long delay.
Change is sensor change: true thermal unchanged but reported y offset/gain/noise changed; E5 reaches 0.105 ambient and steps ~0.0054 match baseline, E6 shape not offset copy of E1.
